parsed.explanation: No law criminalises trans identity or presentation, and discrimination on grounds of gender reassignment remains protected, with functioning courts and active litigation — positives. But the documented exposures are state-imposed and universal: strip-searching by birth sex in transport and regional police policy, legal permission to exclude trans people from single-sex services (statutory code in force Aug 2026), prison/custody placement by birth sex upheld at first instance, announced hospital-ward bans, and the Joelle case showing ward denial contributed to a death. Those are tier-1 exposures with only partial, unresolved recourse, while media climate is hostile. No documented border friction or visitor-targeted violence, so not lower; custody/facility/care risk caps it in the Elevated band.
